newsitem.title: GERMANY: Duesseldorf passengers down 4.8pct 1996 after fire.
newsitem.headline: Duesseldorf passengers down 4.8pct 1996 after fire.

text.p: A downturn in domestic passenger numbers and the impact of last April's fire disaster led to a 4.8 percent drop to 14.4 million passengers last year, Flughafen Duesseldorf GmbH said.
Duesseldorf (DUS) has now fallen back to third-largest German airport status behind Frankfurt and Munich from second place.
The April 11 fire which killed 17 people and led to months of temporary handling arrangements including massive check-in tents had a clear impact, the airport acknowledged.
A spokesman told Reuters: "It could be that some passengers are avoiding Duesseldorf because they do not know that the airport has now improved.
"Some people still do not know that the tents are no longer here," he added.
The airport opened two interim passenger handling halls in November but a long-term re-building programme is planned.

It was also unclear whether passengers had transferred to other airports such as nearby Cologne or switched to rail and other forms of transport, the spokesman added. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44-171-542-7706 Fax +5017
